issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify an addGuestStudents method with a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)), and the solution implements addGuestStudents(int). However, the template defines addGuestStudents with a different signature that includes an extra boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int, boolean)). This parameter mismatch is structural and will confuse students about which method to implement and how to call it.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's method signature match the specification and solution by changing the template to declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO */ }. Alternatively, if the boolean validateInput parameter is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to require addGuestStudents(int, boolean) and update the solution accordingly.

issues.description: The template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with the signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) while the problem statement and the solution implementation expect addGuestStudents(int). This parameter mismatch creates a direct API inconsistency: students reading the task will look for or implement addGuestStudents(int) but the provided template forces a different method signature, causing confusion when mapping requirements to the starter code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution by removing the extra boolean parameter. Replace the template declaration with: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* ... */ } and update any comments to indicate validation should be implemented inside the method body if needed.
